title: [C12T3] - Patterns of Fast Food Restaurant Visits in the USA
prompt: The chart below shows how frequently people in the USA ate in fast food restaurants between 2003 and 2013. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features and making comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart illustrates how often people in the United States ate at fast food restaurants across three different years: 2003, 2006, and 2013.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the data shows that most categories experienced fluctuations rather than consistent trends throughout the period. In addition, eating at fast food restaurants "once a week" and "once or twice a month" remained the two most common frequencies across all three years.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the most frequent eating patterns, in 2003, approximately 31% of Americans ate at fast food restaurants once a week, which was slightly higher than those who dined once or twice a month, at around 30%. The former category saw a notable increase to roughly 33% in 2006, before declining to about 28% by 2013. Similarly, the latter group experienced fluctuations, dropping to approximately 25% in 2006, finally peaking at roughly 33% in the final year.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the remaining categories, in 2003, about 16% of people ate at fast food restaurants several times a week, while around 13% did so only a few times a year. Both categories showed relatively minor changes over the decade, with the former reaching approximately 20% in 2006 before falling back to about 16% in 2013, while the latter remained fairly stable at around 14-15% throughout the period. Meanwhile, the proportions of daily fast food consumers and those who never ate at such establishments remained consistently low, both fluctuating between 3-4% across all three years.
